analyst_view.overall: Early view: Córdoba (11th) under Iván Ania play open games (22 scored, 22 conceded) and have improved recently, with Percan their main scorer on six goals. Second-placed Castellón under Pablo Hernández have the best defence in the league (5 conceded in 12) and a game in hand against Eibar that was postponed after the death of Jesús de Miguel and still has no date, which could add December fixtures. Matías Orozco's ban from his red card will be served well before this date.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals. Córdoba's matches are open, but Castellón have let in only five all season, so I lean a little lower and expect something closer to two or three goals.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.3 corners. Córdoba at home should push forward and Castellón are comfortable defending, which fits the number, so I have no reason to move.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.2 cards. That is already a high figure and the referee is not known yet, so I stay with it.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.9 shots. Córdoba create plenty at home and Castellón's attack, with Adam Jakobsen and Orozco, is one of the best, so I stay with the number.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.7 shots on target. Castellón's defence and goalkeeper Romain Matthys have kept most sides to very few clear chances, so I lean slightly lower.
